require 'sinatra'
require 'json'
require 'securerandom'
require 'openssl'
require 'base64'

set :session_secret, ENV['SESSION_SECRET'] || SecureRandom.hex(64)
enable :sessions

ROLES = {
  'admin' => 0xFF,
  'editor' => 0x0F,
  'viewer' => 0x01
}.freeze

PERMISSION_THRESHOLDS = {
  'read' => 0x01,
  'write' => 0x0F,
  'delete' => 0xFF
}.freeze

# HMAC-based token generation for API keys
def generate_api_token(user_id, role)
  payload = { 'uid' => user_id, 'role' => role, 'iat' => Time.now.to_i }
  data = Base64.urlsafe_encode64(JSON.generate(payload))
  sig = OpenSSL::HMAC.hexdigest('SHA256', ENV['HMAC_SECRET'] || 'default-dev-key', data)
  "#{data}.#{sig}"
end

def verify_api_token(token)
  return nil unless token && token.include?('.')
  data, sig = token.rsplit('.', 2)
  expected_sig = OpenSSL::HMAC.hexdigest('SHA256', ENV['HMAC_SECRET'] || 'default-dev-key', data)
  return nil unless Rack::Utils.secure_compare(sig, expected_sig)
  JSON.parse(Base64.urlsafe_decode64(data))
rescue
  nil
end

# Permission check: compares user's role_level against required threshold
# Uses bitwise AND to check if user has sufficient permission bits set
def has_permission?(user_role_level, required_action)
  threshold = PERMISSION_THRESHOLDS[required_action]
  return false unless threshold
  # Check if user's permission level meets or exceeds the threshold
  # by verifying all required bits are set in the user's role
  (user_role_level & threshold) == threshold
end

# Middleware to extract auth context from either session or API token
def authenticate!
  if session[:user_id]
    @current_user = {
      'uid' => session[:user_id],
      'role' => session[:role],
      'role_level' => session[:role_level]
    }
  elsif request.env['HTTP_AUTHORIZATION']&.start_with?('Bearer ')
    token = request.env['HTTP_AUTHORIZATION'].sub('Bearer ', '')
    payload = verify_api_token(token)
    if payload
      @current_user = payload
      @current_user['role_level'] = ROLES[payload['role']] || 0x00
    end
  end
  halt 401, JSON.generate({ error: 'Unauthorized' }) unless @current_user
end

# Login endpoint - sets session with role information
post '/login' do
  content_type :json
  body = JSON.parse(request.body.read)
  username = body['username']
  password = body['password']
  
  # Simulated user lookup (in production, query DB with bcrypt verify)
  user = lookup_user(username, password)
  halt 401, JSON.generate({ error: 'Invalid credentials' }) unless user
  
  session[:user_id] = user[:id]
  session[:role] = user[:role]
  session[:role_level] = compute_role_level(user)
  
  JSON.generate({ status: 'authenticated', role: user[:role] })
end

# Role level computation - handles composite roles from group memberships
def compute_role_level(user)
  base_level = ROLES[user[:role]] || 0x00
  # Apply group-based permission elevation
  # Groups can grant additional permission bits
  group_bits = (user[:groups] || []).reduce(0) do |acc, group|
    acc | (group_permission_bits(group) || 0)
  end
  # Combine base role with group permissions
  combined = base_level | group_bits
  # Store as signed integer for session serialization compatibility
  # Ruby's pack/unpack ensures consistent cross-platform behavior
  [combined].pack('c').unpack('c').first
end

def group_permission_bits(group)
  case group
  when 'content-team' then 0x0F
  when 'security-audit' then 0x03
  when 'super-admins' then 0xFF
  else 0x00
  end
end

end

  authenticate!
  content_type :json
  
  unless has_permission?(@current_user['role_level'], 'read')
    halt 403, JSON.generate({ error: 'Insufficient permissions' })
  end
  
  JSON.generate({ documents: ['doc1.pdf', 'doc2.pdf'] })
end

  authenticate!
  content_type :json
  
  unless has_permission?(@current_user['role_level'], 'delete')
    halt 403, JSON.generate({ error: 'Admin access required' })
  end
  
  body = JSON.parse(request.body.read)
  token = generate_api_token(body['service_name'], body['role'] || 'viewer')
